flashcard_questions.q: What are the building blocks that make up protein?
How many of the 20 amino acids are essential and must come from food?
What makes a protein high biological value (HBV)?
flashcard_questions.a: It contains all eight essential amino acids.

flashcard_questions.q: Which plant protein source is HBV rather than LBV?

flashcard_questions.a: Combining two or more LBV protein sources in a meal so together they supply all eight essential amino acids.

flashcard_questions.q: In beans on toast, which food group complements the pulses?
How much energy does protein provide per gram?
What is the reference nutrient intake (RNI) for protein in adults?
flashcard_questions.a: 0.75 g per kilogram of bodyweight per day.

flashcard_questions.q: What protein value do the reference intakes on food labels use for an average adult?
What protein deficiency disease causes a swollen abdomen, thinning hair and skin lesions?

flashcard_questions.a: The liver breaking down excess amino acids, turning the nitrogen part into urea.

flashcard_questions.q: Which organ excretes the urea made when excess protein is broken down?
Mycoprotein, sold as Quorn, is grown from which fungus?

flashcard_questions.a: By curdling soya milk and pressing the curds into blocks.

flashcard_questions.q: What is TVP (textured vegetable protein) made from?
flashcard_questions.a: Soya flour processed into a chewy, meat-like texture.

notes: 15 cards: 7 term/concept, 3 value cards (4 kcal/g, RNI 0.75 g/kg, label RI 50 g), 2 deficiency/process (kwashiorkor, deamination), 3 source/product cards (soya, Fusarium venenatum, tofu). Dropped the eight named essential amino acids as an enumeration; kept the count instead. Complementation covered forward only (term to definition plus one worked pairing), never both directions.
